To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the diversity gain is equal to the number of antennas at the relay and the multiplexing loss approaches one when the SNR decreases to infinity.
the f-DMT for TWRCs with multi-antennas is a non-decreasing function of the number of relay antenna.
the f-DMT of the considered TWRC is characterized by two parameters: the multiplexing and diversity gains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the finite-SNR DTM for TWRC with multi-antennas.
the finite-SNR DTM of two-way relay systems with multiple antennas at the relay.
the fundamental tradeoffs between diversity gain, multiplexing gain and SNR in TWRC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the relay location and time sharing play a more significant role on the outage probability and f-DMTs than the rate allocation does.
the relay location has a great impact on the f-DMT, and the optimal relay location is the midpoint of the two source nodes.
, for a given number of relay antennas, the TWRC has a higher outage probability and a better f-DMT than the corresponding one-way relaying channel (OWRC).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have provided a complete f-DMT framework for the multi-antenna TWRC, which can be used for performance analysis, design optimization and protocol selection.
the f-DMT of a multi-antenna TWRC is determined by the number of relay antenna, time sharing, rate and relay location.
the outage probability of the considered two-way relay system is well characterized by the derived upper and lower bounds, which are very tight for a broad range of SNR values.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the outage and fDMT of TWRC can be significantly improved by using multiple antennas at relay.
, in contrast to the infinite-SNR DMT analysis, the relay location and time sharing do not affect the f-DMT of TWRCs with multiple antennas at the relay.
the f-DMT can be improved by increasing the relay location and decreasing the time sharing factor.
